extracted.intended_audience: students and instructors of algebraic geometry (advanced undergraduates / graduate students) and self-learners
extracted.subtask_description: Conventions, pedagogical goals, prerequisites, and reading guidance for a foundational textbook in algebraic geometry intended as a (challenging) first-year course or for serious self-study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ring conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: All rings are assumed to be commutative unless explicitly stated otherwise. All rings are assumed to contain a unit, denoted 1. Maps of rings must send 1 to 1; in other words, the “0-ring” (with one element) is allowed. The definition of “integral domain” includes 1 ≠ 0, so the 0-ring is not an integral domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are book-wide foundational conventions: expect ring maps to preserve 1, and note the treatment of the 0-ring and the integral domain convention when reading proofs and statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisite mathematical background
rubrics_metrics.description: The reader should be familiar with some basic notions in commutative ring theory, in particular the notion of ideals (including prime and maximal ideals) and localization. Tensor products and exact sequences of A-modules will be important. Use notation (A,m) or (A,m,k) for local rings. The structure theorem for finitely generated modules over a PID is used. Some experience with field theory will be helpful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This textbook aims to minimize prerequisites but expects comfort with the listed algebraic notions; topology exposure is also 'certainly essential' for intuition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of the Axiom of Choice
rubrics_metrics.description: The book accepts the Axiom of Choice. In particular, any proper ideal in a ring is contained in a maximal ideal. The Axiom of Choice also arises in arguments such as that the category of A-modules has enough injectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers who are cautious about set-theoretic/foundational issues are referred to specialized references; proofs and some constructions assume AC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Starred sections reading policy
rubrics_metrics.description: There are optional starred sections marked with a star: ⋆. Starred sections are topics worth knowing on a second or third (but not first) reading. Double-starred sections (⋆⋆) you should not read unless you really really want to, but you should be aware of their existence. Starred sections are not necessarily harder, merely unimportant for first pass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the stars to prioritize reading: skip double-starred material on a first pass; return to single-starred material later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary pedagogical goals and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The core of the material should be digestible over a single year. After a year readers should have a broad familiarity with the foundations of the subject and be ready to attend seminars and learn more advanced material. The book seeks to cover a canon completely and rigorously, with enough examples and calculations to develop intuition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book is intentionally not encyclopedic; analytic aspects are essentially ignored. Instructors will choose which 'inessential' topics to include in a course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-contained presentation and proof requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The book is intended to be as self-contained as possible. The motto: 'if you use it, you must prove it.' The book develops facts quickly from scratch when needed so readers can see what's involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This choice makes the book denser and demands more maturity from the reader, but reduces external prerequisites and prevents relying on remote references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercises central to learning
rubrics_metrics.description: The exercises are central for building intuition. Informal language and many examples are given to help develop intuition for the machinery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Working through exercises is essential to achieve the book's learning goals; they are not peripheral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended learning mode
rubrics_metrics.description: The book is usable for a course, but most mortals cannot learn algebraic geometry fully on their own; ideally you should read in a group and have someone to ask questions to (both stupid and smart questions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For self-study, seek peers or mentors; courses can adopt the book but should take on the instructor's personality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation and nonmathematical conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonmathematical conventions are stated (e.g., 'Unimportant' means 'unimportant for the current exposition', not necessarily unimportant generally). Local ring notation and other idiosyncratic uses are specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be alert to the author's idiosyncratic terminology and local notation choices when reading statements and proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference to introduce certain technical hypotheses early
rubrics_metrics.description: The book opts to introduce notions like quasiseparatedness early (instead of relying on Noetherian hypotheses). Quasiseparatedness 'comes up early and often' — the cost is one extra word to remember, but it helps: whenever 'quasicompact and quasiseparated' turn up the reader will immediately guess a key idea of the proof. Similarly, distinguish coherent sheaves and finite type (quasicoherent) sheaves in statements even though they coincide in the Noetherian situation to be clearer on what is used in proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect the author to favor explicit, sometimes more general hypotheses to clarify proofs rather than assuming stronger but less general hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberate omissions and optional coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Many important topics are not discussed or are optional: valuative criteria are not proved and their statement is relegated to an optional section; omitted topics include d´evissage, formal schemes, and cohomology with supports. Analytic aspects are essentially ignored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect encyclopedic coverage; consult other references for omitted or analytic material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of aims and compromises
rubrics_metrics.description: The book tries to do a few things well (rigorous canonical coverage with examples and exercises) and explicitly gives up other desiderata; instructors and readers must accept compromises to reconcile completeness with accessibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate trade-offs (density vs prerequisites, generality vs simplicity) in choices throughout the book.
